basis: Cataracts, skin/hair disease and oral inflammation define syndrome; myopathy in 1/1 assessed patient. Developmental delay in 1/2 omitted by cap.
Mycobacterial infection defined by anesthetic skin lesions and early peripheral nerve injury.
Micrognathia, glossoptosis and cleft palate define sequence; upper airway obstruction affects 30-79%. Erroneous ocular ancestry does not establish eye disease.
Adipose neoplasm arising in skin or subcutis.
Corticospinal tract degeneration defines pure spastic paraplegia; weakness is neurogenic, and urinary symptoms do not establish urinary tract damage.
Progressive palmoplantar keratoderma; flexion contractures and digital autoamputation are each reported in 30-79%, causing structural locomotor impairment.
Generalized epilepsy is a disorder of brain function.
Inherited erythroid marrow failure; specified renal and cardiac malformations occur in 5-29%, and other anomalies lack evidence of a 30% frequency.
Cerebellar degeneration with cognitive, pyramidal and sensory dysfunction; nystagmus reflects neurologic dysfunction rather than intrinsic eye damage.
Fatty acid oxidation defect with myopathy/rhabdomyolysis; neuropathy and cardiomyopathy each 30-79%. Hepatic disease, also 30-79%, omitted by cap; retinopathy <30%.
Hepatic bilirubin conjugation defect causes benign unconjugated hyperbilirubinemia without hepatocellular injury.
Chronic inflammatory polyradiculoneuropathy affects peripheral nerves and roots; the term generally denotes immune-mediated demyelinating disease.
Ependymal neoplasm arising in the central nervous system.
Malignancy occupying major salivary glands; lymphoma is only one minority histologic subtype and does not define the umbrella.
Renal tubular sodium transport disorder defined by hypertension and hypokalemic metabolic alkalosis, each documented in 3/3 patients.
Complement-mediated glomerular injury defines disease. Hypertension is secondary; visual impairment is occasional, and retinal deposits alone do not qualify.
HIV-associated syndrome defined by major muscle wasting with myofiber degeneration; malabsorption indicates gastrointestinal loss of function in 30-79%.
Membrane-stabilizing drug poisoning produces cardiac conduction impairment, arrhythmias and shock, with characteristic CNS toxicity including seizures or coma.
Intellectual disability, developmental delay and seizures define the neurodevelopmental disorder; hypotonia alone does not establish muscle disease.
Anemia defined by reduced hemoglobin content of red blood cells.
Retinal degeneration, deafness and obesity define syndrome; hypopituitarism is frequent. Intellectual disability occurs in 5/5 assessed patients.
Impaired cardiac pump function defines disease; congestion and pulmonary edema do not establish direct intrinsic lung injury.
Renal amyloid deposition causes progressive renal failure; frequent hepatic and pulmonary deposits are usually subclinical without demonstrated functional injury.
Brain atrophy, epilepsy and profound developmental impairment define disease; sensorineural hearing impairment occurs in 2/6 patients (~33%).
Congenital mitral inflow obstruction from a supravalvular ring; pulmonary edema is hemodynamic, and pulmonary hypertension remains cardiovascular.
